card.intuition: The instructions the harness prepends to every model provider request — the agent's standing brief: who it is, how to behave, which tools it can call, and what conventions to follow. Usually stable across a session, it forms the start of the prefix cache and is re-paid as input tokens on every turn.
card.analogy: An employee handbook tucked on top of every memo a staffer writes: it defines the role and rules and is identical on every request, so it's cached rather than rewritten; your project's AGENTS.md rides along beside it.
card.time_complexity: The model re-reads the entire context on every turn, so cost and latency grow with context size per request.
card.space_complexity: System prompts are often tens of thousands of tokens; they consume context-window budget on every request before user content begins.
when_to_use: Investigating divergent behavior between harnesses sharing the same model
Reading or customizing the system prompt where a harness exposes it
Expecting your own standing instructions (AGENTS.md) to load alongside the vendor brief
gotchas: Models are trained to prioritize the system prompt over user messages — an unwanted convention may come from it and out-argue your message
It's paid as input tokens every turn, so a huge system prompt raises the cost of every single request

steps.label: Prepare
steps.annotation: The harness composes the standing system prompt describing role, tools, and rules.

steps.label: Append yours
steps.annotation: Project instructions are loaded next to it before the user's message arrives.

steps.label: Request
steps.annotation: The full system prompt is prepended to every model provider request.

steps.label: Cache
steps.annotation: Being identical each turn, it anchors the prefix cache across requests.

steps.label: Prioritize
steps.annotation: The model reads and weights the system prompt above user messages.

exercise.prompt: Build the request the harness actually sends: system prompt plus the user message in a convention the model expects.
exercise.starter_code:
def build_request(system_prompt, user_message):
    prompt = system_prompt + "

USER:
" + user_message
    return ___________
hints: The system prompt always comes first, before the user's message.
Return the fully assembled request string that gets sent to the provider.
exercise.test_code:
p = build_request("# You are a careful reviewer", "Summarize this PR")
assert p.startswith("# You are a careful reviewer")
assert "USER:" in p
assert "Summarize this PR" in p
print('PASS')
